paper_title: CtD: Composition through Decomposition in Emergent Communication
summary:
CtD: Composition through Decomposition in Emergent Communication - Boaz Carmeli, Ron Meir, Yonatan Belinkov, 2025

Carmeli, Meir, and Belinkov target the persistent failure mode in emergent communication where discrete channels and standard referential games yield high task accuracy without systematic compositional structure. Their objective is to induce agents to generalize to unseen concept combinations by first forcing them to recover atomic concepts from complex observations, rather than learning composition directly in a single-stage game. The proposed CtD pipeline separates learning into a DECOMPOSE phase and a COMPOSE phase. In DECOMPOSE, sender and receiver play a multi target coordination game over objects represented by feature value pairs or images, and the sender maps observations into a discrete codebook learned with vector quantization style latent discretization. In COMPOSE, the same codebook is reused in a standard referential game so that messages become sequences of previously grounded codewords corresponding to basic concepts. The implementation compares three communication mechanisms, Gumbel Softmax, quantized communication, and explicit codebook based communication, and evaluates on five datasets spanning synthetic symbolic objects, SHAPE, MNIST digit pairs, COCO derived concepts, and a non compositional QRC control set. The paper measures both task success and structure using ACC, AMI, POS, BOS, CI, and CBM, with CBM and CI used to verify one to one concept to code alignment and message level compositionality. ([belinkov.com](https://belinkov.com/assets/pdf/iclr2025-ctd.pdf))

The concrete result is that pretraining a discrete concept inventory through multi target decomposition is the decisive ingredient: on THING, codebook based CtD reaches ACC 1.00, AMI 1.00, CI 1.00, and CBM 1.00 on composite phrases, versus 0.25 ACC, 0.16 AMI, 0.03 CI, and 0.25 CBM when composing without decomposition. On SHAPE, CtD reaches 0.99 ACC with CI 1.00 and CBM 1.00, compared with 0.26 ACC and 0.47 CBM without decomposition. On MNIST, CtD improves from 0.41 to 0.81 ACC and from 0.58 to 0.95 CBM, while zero shot transfer from SINGLE CONCEPT training to COMPOSITE PHRASE evaluation attains 0.89 ACC, 0.97 CI, and 0.96 CBM, exceeding the trained CtD accuracy on that dataset. Zero shot performance is also perfect on THING and remains strong on SHAPE at 0.81 ACC with CI and CBM both 1.00, showing that once the codebook is grounded, composition can emerge with little or no additional optimization. Ablations show that collapsing DECOMPOSE from multi target to single target leaves accuracy largely intact but drives compositional metrics toward random, and codebook analysis on SHAPE shows exact one concept to one index usage with CBM 1.00 over 1000 test samples and maximum inter code similarity only 0.35. The method does not help on the non compositional QRC benchmark, where zero shot ACC drops to 0.48 and CtD slightly underperforms direct training, supporting the claim that CtD specifically exploits compositional latent structure rather than acting as a generic pretraining heuristic. ([belinkov.com](https://belinkov.com/assets/pdf/iclr2025-ctd.pdf))
